messages.author: b580f6ffa202c87e
messages.subject: Model comparison
parts:
Hello Everyone, 

I'm building hierarchical Bayesian time series model and interested in comparing different orders of the model to find the best fit. I tried using the WAIC in NimbleMCMC. I get a negative WAIC value and also a warning stating that: There are individual pWAIC values that are greater than 0.4. This may indicate that the WAIC estimate is unstable (Vehtari et al., 2017), at least in cases without grouping of data nodes or multivariate data nodes.

I understand that getting a negative WAIC value is not an issue but was wondering if I can still use the WAIC value obtained from this model for model comparison purposes due to the warning. I saw a demo for the nimblecarbon package where they also get the same warning for the WAIC but have still used it comparison. I did look at the Vehtari paper but it still is not very clear. 

Any advise/suggestions on this will be greatly appreciated. If i cannot use this, then is there any other model comparison techniques which NIMBLE provides that I can use. 

Thank you in advance.

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Model comparison
parts:
Hi Sreeram,

Our warning is based on the guidance in the Vehtari paper, and we don't have additional insight into how much of a problem values greater than 0.4 are.
My suggestion would be to run your MCMC chain longer to see if that causes the individual pWAIC values to decrease. You may also want to check that
your burn-in period is sufficiently long.

-Chris

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Model comparison
parts:
Unfortunately, I can't say whether it is ok. I'll also note that how to think about WAIC with correlated data (such as time series)
may be tricky - please see our documentation (manual and R help information) for some discussion of different forms of WAIC
related to how to group data in terms of what is considered an "observation".

You could also consider doing cross-validation. 

-Chris

Best,
